items.title: Establish one canonical Jordan 191 handling scene and Monaco GP2-style acceptance matrix
items.description: Select one canonical vehicle (Jordan 191) and one repeatable handling scene; define behavior-first acceptance tests covering progressive turn-in, recoverable oversteer, entry understeer when overdriven, stable straight-line braking, short transient settling, manageable curbs, and clearly greater high-speed stability than low-speed stability. Mostly scene/source-of-truth cleanup and test definition; do not change physics parameters until the canonical route is bootable and repeatable.
items.rationale: The repository currently has multiple vehicle baselines: test_field.tscn still instantiates f1_1996_car.tscn, while jordan_191.tscn is the intended 1990s single-seater baseline, and the previous backlog referenced non-existent jordan_1995/jordan_handling_test paths. Before tuning, select one canonical vehicle and one repeatable handling scene.
items.technical_risk: Low-medium. This is mostly scene/source-of-truth cleanup and test definition. Avoid changing physics parameters until the canonical route is bootable and repeatable.
items.user_value: Creates a single authoritative car and test loop so every subsequent handling change is comparable and intentional.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical car is selected (jordan_191.tscn) and test_field.tscn routes through it (no f1_1996_car.tscn instantiation remains in the bootstrap path).

Acceptance matrix is documented with the seven behavior-first criteria: progressive turn-in, recoverable oversteer, entry understeer when overdriven, stable straight-line braking, short transient settling, manageable curbs, greater high-speed stability than low-speed stability.
Handling scene is bootable and repeatable without parameter tuning side effects.
evidence: Backlog pruned for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Backlog pruned for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Normalize the canonical 1990s F1 physical envelope (mass, CG, track and wheel geometry)
items.description: Merge the old tire-width, track-width and tire-radius tasks into one sanity pass over mass, CG, track and wheel geometry. Use plausible 1990s F1 values constrained by the actual Jordan 191 model dimensions; do not pursue millimeter-perfect historical homologation. Change the minimum coherent set once, then freeze it before behavioral tuning.
items.rationale: Steering, suspension, load transfer and tire tuning are unreliable if the basic physical envelope is not formula-like. Merge the old tire-width, track-width and tire-radius tasks into one sanity pass. Use plausible 1990s F1 values and the actual Jordan 191 model dimensions as constraints; do not pursue millimeter-perfect historical homologation.
items.technical_risk: Medium. These values affect grip, Ackermann, gearing and weight transfer simultaneously. Change the minimum coherent set once, then freeze it before behavioral tuning.
items.user_value: Removes GT-like geometric assumptions before handling tuning without turning the task into a historical reconstruction project.
acceptance_criteria: Mass, CG, track widths and wheel dimensions on jordan_191.tscn are set to a coherent 1990s F1 envelope derived from the model dimensions, not from later-era GT values.
No Phase A/B physical parameter outside mass, CG, track and wheel geometry is changed in the same commit.
Runtime values are documented and frozen before subsequent handling tuning.
evidence: Merged PHY-003/PHY-004/PHY-005 for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Merged PHY-003/PHY-004/PHY-005 for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Define the canonical assist policy and remove undocumented stabilization from handling tests
items.description: Establish the exact baseline assist state for the canonical car: Monaco GP2-style handling may use mild intentional steering/countersteer assistance, but every assist that affects yaw, wheelspin or braking must be explicit and reproducible. Do not compensate by retuning multiple subsystems at once.
items.rationale: The canonical handling baseline must not be tuned against unknown hidden stabilization. Monaco GP2-style handling may use mild intentional steering/countersteer assistance, but every assist that affects yaw, wheelspin or braking must be explicit and reproducible. Establish the exact baseline assist state before tuning.
items.technical_risk: Medium. Removing or changing assists can expose underlying instability; do not compensate by retuning multiple subsystems at once.
items.user_value: Makes the car's behavior intentional: approachable arcade-sim assistance is allowed, but hidden physics compensation is not.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical assist state is documented for yaw, wheelspin and braking aids.
No undocumented stabilization is observable during the handling acceptance matrix.
Aids can be toggled reproducibly without code changes.
evidence: Reframed from precise OFF semantics into a short-term canonical baseline requirement, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Reframed from precise OFF semantics into a short-term canonical baseline requirement, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Reproduce and fix automatic-transmission top-out or incomplete shift progression
items.description: Reproduce the reported second-gear top-out using the canonical scene and current ratios. If confirmed, fix only the shift-condition defect; do not redesign the transmission. Verify all forward gears and downshifts after the minimal fix.
items.rationale: A canonical car cannot be evaluated if automatic shifting fails to reach the full gearbox. Reproduce the reported second-gear top-out using the canonical scene and current ratios. If confirmed, fix only the shift-condition defect; do not redesign the transmission.
items.technical_risk: Low-medium. The change can alter engine/gear interaction, so verify all forward gears and downshifts after the minimal fix.
items.user_value: Ensures the car can complete full-speed handling tests and later race sessions without a basic drivetrain blocker.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduction of the second-gear top-out is documented using the canonical scene.
If the defect is confirmed, the minimal fix is applied to the shift condition only.
All forward gears and downshifts are validated after the fix.
evidence: Promoted as a blocking reproducibility/fix task for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Promoted as a blocking reproducibility/fix task for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Tune canonical F1 steering, yaw response and countersteer progression
items.description: Target a late-1990s arcade-sim formula feel: quick but progressive turn-in, low rotational inertia, mild entry understeer when overdriven, progressive throttle/lift-off rotation, and recoverable oversteer when countersteer is applied early. Steering assist, tire response and yaw damping are coupled; tune one behavior family at a time against the acceptance matrix.
items.rationale: The current car is described as halfway between a GT3 and excessive oversteer. Target a late-1990s arcade-sim formula feel: quick but progressive turn-in, low rotational inertia, mild entry understeer when overdriven, progressive throttle/lift-off rotation, and recoverable oversteer when countersteer is applied early.
items.technical_risk: High. Steering assist, tire response and yaw damping are coupled. Tune one behavior family at a time against the acceptance matrix.
items.user_value: This is the core 'it feels like an F1 car' milestone and the highest-value handling change.
acceptance_criteria: Steering satisfies the acceptance matrix: progressive turn-in, mild entry understeer when overdriven, progressive throttle/lift-off rotation, recoverable oversteer.
Countersteer applied early recovers the car; late countersteer still rotates it.
Tuning is documented per behavior family (assist, tire, yaw damping).
evidence: Retargeted from exact 1995 steering to Monaco GP2-style canonical F1 feel, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Retargeted from exact 1995 steering to Monaco GP2-style canonical F1 feel, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Tune canonical F1 suspension, transient weight transfer and curb stability
items.description: Remove the GT3-like sense of mass and long body settling. The car should react sharply, roll little, settle quickly after braking or direction changes, remain stable under straight braking, and tolerate normal curbs without random launches or persistent bottom-out. Historical damper values are not required; suspension changes must not mask tire, geometry or track-collision problems.
items.rationale: Remove the GT3-like sense of mass and long body settling. The car should react sharply, roll little, settle quickly after braking or direction changes, remain stable under straight braking, and tolerate normal curbs without random launches or persistent bottom-out. Historical damper values are not required.
items.technical_risk: High. Suspension changes can mask tire, geometry or track-collision problems. Use the existing diagnostic guardrails only when a concrete symptom appears.
items.user_value: Creates the short, stiff, responsive chassis behavior expected from a single-seater instead of a heavy GT car.
acceptance_criteria: Suspension produces short transient settling (no long body settling).
Stable under straight braking.
Normal curbs are tolerated without random launches or persistent bottom-out.
Tire, geometry and track-collision symptoms are checked before any damper/spring change.
evidence: Retargeted from exact 1995 suspension values to behavior-first canonical handling, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Retargeted from exact 1995 suspension values to behavior-first canonical handling, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Add a simple speed-squared aero balance with a clear low-speed/high-speed handling transition
items.description: Add the minimum tunable V^2 downforce model needed so low-speed behavior is primarily mechanical and lively while medium/high-speed corners become distinctly more planted. Keep front/rear balance and drag simple; no CFD, ground-effect simulation or historical aero map. Implement only after steering and suspension are acceptable at low/medium speed.
items.rationale: A formula car should not feel like a lightweight GT at every speed. Add the minimum tunable V^2 downforce model needed so low-speed behavior is primarily mechanical and lively while medium/high-speed corners become distinctly more planted. Keep front/rear balance and drag simple; no CFD, ground-effect simulation or historical aero map.
items.technical_risk: High. Aero can hide bad mechanical balance. Implement only after steering and suspension are acceptable at low/medium speed.
items.user_value: Provides one of the strongest perceptual cues that the vehicle is an F1-style single-seater.
acceptance_criteria: Downforce scales with V^2 and is configurable.
No downforce is applied at rest/low speed (mechanical behavior unchanged).
Low-speed behavior is primarily mechanical and lively; medium/high-speed corners are distinctly more planted.
Front/rear balance and drag are exposed for tuning.
evidence: Simplified from historical Phase F aero into the minimum model needed for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Simplified from historical Phase F aero into the minimum model needed for Canonical F1 Handling v1, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Tune the canonical high-rev V10 powertrain and close-ratio gearbox as one package
items.description: Tune fast rev response, strong top-end character, useful engine braking, shift cadence and close ratios together. The deterministic per-gear speed and shift-point checks are acceptance criteria for this task; they are not separate backlog features. Preserve the working GEVP ownership model.
items.rationale: Powertrain character must support the F1 identity without becoming an engine-simulation project. Tune fast rev response, strong top-end character, useful engine braking, shift cadence and close ratios together. Fold the old separate gearbox and offline powertrain-validation items into this task; deterministic per-gear speed/shift checks are acceptance criteria, not separate backlog features.
items.technical_risk: Medium-high. Torque curve, inertia, clutch, final drive and shift thresholds interact; preserve the working GEVP ownership model.
items.user_value: Adds the high-revving, closely geared response expected from a late-1990s-style Formula car.
acceptance_criteria: Torque curve has strong top-end character and fast rev response.
Engine braking is useful and tactically exploitable.
Per-gear top speed and shift-RPM are documented offline (analyze_powertrain.py) and reproduced at runtime.
Close-ratio gearbox with correct overlap/shift cadence is implemented together with the engine curve.
evidence: Merged PHY-008/PHY-009/PHY-011 into one short-term powertrain package, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Merged PHY-008/PHY-009/PHY-011 into one short-term powertrain package, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Freeze Canonical F1 Handling v1 and capture a lightweight regression baseline
items.description: Once steering, suspension, aero and powertrain satisfy the Monaco GP2-style acceptance matrix, stop major handling work. Record the final setup plus a small repeatable telemetry set for low-speed rotation, braking, direction change, fast corner, curb and full-gear acceleration. Goal: regression protection, not a telemetry platform.
items.rationale: Once steering, suspension, aero and powertrain satisfy the Monaco GP2-style acceptance matrix, stop major handling work. Record the final setup plus a small repeatable telemetry set for low-speed rotation, braking, direction change, fast corner, curb and full-gear acceleration. The goal is regression protection, not a telemetry platform.
items.technical_risk: Low. Avoid building immutable telemetry infrastructure or a generalized analytics system; a small versioned baseline is sufficient.
items.user_value: Prevents endless physics tuning and establishes the canonical car that track, AI and race systems can safely target.
acceptance_criteria: Final setup values are recorded in PROJECT_STATE.md and on the canonical scene.
A small versioned telemetry set covers low-speed rotation, braking, direction change, fast corner, curb and full-gear acceleration.
No immutable telemetry infrastructure is introduced; a versioned baseline is sufficient.
evidence: Rewritten from telemetry-provenance infrastructure into a minimal handling-freeze gate, 2026-08-11.
items.source_context: Rewritten from telemetry-provenance infrastructure into a minimal handling-freeze gate, 2026-08-11.

items.title: Build RaceSession MVP: countdown, checkpoints, lap timing, finish and retry
items.description: After Canonical F1 Handling v1 is frozen, implement truthful race-session state for countdown, checkpoint order, lap count/time, finish and retry/menu. Defer position ranking, opponent roster and rival minimap markers until an actual opponent system exists. Requires one game-state owner and reliable track progression; keep competition/AI out of the MVP.
items.rationale: After Canonical F1 Handling v1 is frozen, the next value milestone is a complete playable loop. Implement truthful race-session state for countdown, checkpoint order, lap count/time, finish and retry/menu. Defer position ranking, opponent roster and rival minimap markers until an actual opponent system exists.
items.technical_risk: Medium. Requires one game-state owner and reliable track progression; keep competition/AI out of the MVP.
items.user_value: Turns the handling prototype into a small complete game mode instead of continuing physics/tooling work indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Countdown, checkpoint order, lap count/time, finish and retry/menu are driven by a single authoritative race-session model.
No placeholder race values are visible in normal gameplay.
Lap transitions are tested around the canonical track start/finish line.
Position ranking and opponent roster remain deferred until an opponent system exists.
evidence: Reduced from lap/position/countdown/rivals into the first post-handling race-loop milestone, 2026-08-11.
